title: Selection sort against insertion sort
instructions:
## Same list, three algorithms

Step through **selection sort** and **insertion sort** on `29, 10, 14, 37, 13`. Selection sort finds the smallest remaining value and swaps it into place. Insertion sort takes the next value and shifts larger values right to make room.

## Do this

1. Count selection sort's comparisons and swaps.
2. Count insertion sort's shifts.
3. Find **five different values** on which insertion sort does **no shifts at all**, and keep them in the input. What does that say about insertion sort on nearly sorted data?
hints: Selection sort always makes about n²/2 comparisons, whatever the order; read `comparisons` on the last step.
A shift happens every time a larger value moves right; read `shifts` on the last step.
Insertion sort shifts nothing when every value is already in order.

realityNote: Insertion sort is O(n) on sorted or nearly sorted input, which is why library sorts (Timsort, introsort) switch to it for small or already-ordered runs.
